newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan groups to launch campaign against torture.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan groups to launch campaign against torture.

text.p: Morocco's independent human rights groups will launch a national campaign against torture after 10 people died in mysterious circumstances while in custody this year, a spokesman said on Tuesday.
"The government reforms concerning human rights were suspended since 1994," Abdelaziz Bennani, head of the Moroccan Organisation of Human Rights (OMDH) told a news conference.

"In fact we noticed that the situation of public liberties has deteriorated, leading to an increase of state violence in which a total of 10 people died in mysterious circumstances while in custody in 1996," he told reporters.
The usual official version was the victim "committed suicide," Bennani said. "No investigation was carried out by the authorities to clarify the cases," he said.

The group said there was "strong evidence that six people at least died under torture and violence this year while in custody." Bannani, a prominent lawyer, said the group was investigating four other deaths.
Officials at the justice and human rights ministry were not immediately available for comment.
Bennani said the OMDH, the Rabat-based Moroccan Human Rights Association and the Moroccan Human Rights League were starting a campaign to put pressure on the government.

"A three-month nationwide campaign to denounce torture in Morocco will be launched soon," he said. "It aims at pushing the authorities to stick to their previous commitments on the respect of human rights."
In a 33-page report the OMDH said more than 50 political detainees, including young Moslem fundamentalists, were held for years in jails in harsh conditions.
In 1992, Morocco introduced in the constitution "its determination to abide by universally recognised human rights" but little was done to meet this commitment, the OMDH added.
